The '''2016–17 Danish Superliga''' season was the 27th season of the [[Denmark|Danish]] [[Danish Superliga|Superliga]], which decides the [[Danish football championship]]. The season was the first with a new league structure in which 14 clubs play each other home and away until the league is split up in championship and relegation play-offs. The new structure was inspired by the one used by the [[Belgian First Division A]] and was approved by the [[Danish Football Association|Danish FA]], [[Dansk Boldspil-Union]], on 28 June 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dbu.dk/Nyheder/2015/Juni/SL_struktur_godkendt|title=DBU's bestyrelse godkender ny struktur for Superligaen|access-date=2015-06-28|archive-date=2019-01-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190112055942/https://www.dbu.dk/Nyheder/2015/Juni/SL_struktur_godkendt|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The fixtures were announced on 6 June 2016.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.superliga.dk/artikel/kampprogrammet-er-klar|title=KAMPPROGRAMMET ER KLAR!|website=www.superliga.dk|date=6 June 2016 |access-date=6 June 2016}}</ref>

==Teams==
[[Hobro IK]] finished the [[2015–16 Danish Superliga|2015–16 season]] in 12th place and was relegated to the [[2016–17 Danish 1st Division|2016–17 1st Division]].

The relegated team was replaced by [[2015–16 Danish 1st Division|2015–16 1st Division]] champions [[Lyngby Boldklub]], while the 2nd and 3rd place teams, [[Silkeborg IF]] and [[AC Horsens]], were promoted to bring the total teams in the league to 14.

On 23 October 2016, the home stadium for [[Odense Boldklub]] changed its name from TRE-FOR Park to [[EWII Park]] as a consequence of the current stadium sponsor changing its name.<ref name="treforpark-to-ewiipark">{{cite web|last1=Bøttger |first1=Andreas |title=TREFOR Park skifter navn |url=http://www.ob.dk/artikel/trefor-park-skifter-navn.aspx |website=www.ob.dk |publisher=Odense Sport & Event |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120150350/http://www.ob.dk/artikel/trefor-park-skifter-navn.aspx |archive-date=20 November 2016 |language=da |date=3 October 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 31 December 2016, the previous sponsorship agreement for the home stadium of [[AaB Fodbold|Aalborg BK]], Nordjyske Arena, expired, and the stadium was officially referred to as Aalborg Stadium because a new sponsorship agreement was signed and took effect on 1 April 2017, renaming the stadium Aalborg Portland Park.<ref name="nyt-aalborg-portland-park">{{cite web|last1=Lyngdahl |first1=Lars |title=Nyt navn til stadion: Aalborg Portland Park |url=http://www.tv2nord.dk/artikel/nyt-navn-til-stadion-aalborg-portland-park |publisher=TV2 NORD |access-date=19 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170319205144/http://www.tv2nord.dk/artikel/nyt-navn-til-stadion-aalborg-portland-park |archive-date=19 March 2017 |language=da |date=10 March 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
